parts.note: a British reader thinks of the Roman general who invaded Britain in 55 and 54 BC

explanation.surface: A Briton recalls those who have conquered the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius, the Roman general, led the first Roman invasions of Britain, so he counts among its conquerors.

parts.note: in Greek myth the ferryman carried dead souls over the river Styx

explanation.surface: A crossword solver boasts of filling in a clue.

explanation.definitionFit: The ferryman of Greek myth rowed the souls of the dead over the river Styx.

clue.text: Eva here assisted in ' making the escape.

definitions.text: Eva here assisted in ' making the escape.

parts.words: Eva here assisted in ' making the escape
parts.note: if Eva aided, the words run together into a word for getting away

explanation.surface: A woman named Eva helps someone break out.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'Eva aided' runs into the answer, meaning got away.
explanation.definitionFit: Having dodged or escaped from something, one has slipped away from it.

clue.text: These men are of seasoned wisdom.

definitions.text: These men are of seasoned wisdom.

parts.words: These men are of seasoned wisdom
parts.note: wise old men, whose name is also a herb used for seasoning

explanation.walkthrough: The herb sage seasons food, so 'seasoned' plays on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wise men of long experience are the learned elders the word names.

clue.text: A pal would make regal card-houses with these.

definitions.text: A pal would make regal card-houses with these.

parts.note: the top cards of each suit, which joined after a word for friend give a royal residence

explanation.surface: A friend builds fine houses of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: PAL put before the answer makes a regal house, a palace; and the answer is also playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest-ranking playing cards, one in each suit, are single-pip cards.

parts.note: cape as headland, not a garment: an Arabic word for a promontory

explanation.surface: A tailor's verdict on a badly made cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape means a headland, which no one could wear; the word is Arabic, as in place names on the Red Sea coast.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arabic geography it means a headland or promontory, as in many coastal place names.

clue.text: Here the distinguished artist among the beasts of burden produces some sweetmeats.

RA, a Royal Academician, is the crossword's distinguished artist

explanation.walkthrough: 'The distinguished artist' looks like part of the scene, but it is the standard crossword shorthand for a Royal Academician; 'Here' and 'produces' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramels are chewy toffee sweets, and sweetmeat is an old word for a confection.

clue.text: The telephone operator will give you this.

definitions.text: The telephone operator will give you this.

parts.words: The telephone operator will give you this
parts.note: the telephone exchange, which a caller once asked the operator for

explanation.surface: A caller expects to be connected by the switchboard.
explanation.walkthrough: An old name for the telephone exchange, as callers once said 'Hello, Central'.
explanation.definitionFit: Early telephone users called the exchange by this name when asking the operator to connect them.

parts.note: the people of the conqueror named at 1 across came from the city on the Tiber

explanation.surface: A question about where a leader came from.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR dropped the '1' of '1 across': the conqueror there was a citizen of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius, the conqueror, was a citizen of Rome, so that is his people.

parts.note: absent, elsewhere, somewhere other than this place

explanation.surface: A note left on a door.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not present is said to be elsewhere, gone from this place.

clue.text: A winter resort adds tone to its male visitors.

parts.note: Mentone, the old English name of Menton, a Riviera town once popular with winter visitors
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Riviera resort raises the tone of its gentlemen guests.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: MEN 'adds tone' to make MENTONE (Menton, on the French Riviera); 'its' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Male visitors are, in plain words, men, plural to match the clue.

parts.note: the law splits property into land and buildings, and movable goods

explanation.surface: A philosophical shrug about whether something exists or matters.
explanation.walkthrough: In law property is real (land) or personal (goods).
explanation.definitionFit: Property or assets in law, classed as real (land) or personal (movable goods).

clue.text: Here achievement ends very well indeed.

parts.words: Here achievement ends very well indeed
parts.note: the word ends with DID, an achievement, and holds END: an excellent outcome

explanation.surface: A satisfying conclusion to an accomplishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The word contains END and finishes with DID, what an achiever did.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnificent or excellent, said of something done very well.

definitions.meaning: to go away from a place, quitting a room or seat
as a verb, to clear out a house or post so that nobody occupies it

explanation.definitionFit: To vacate is both to go out of a place and to leave it unoccupied, as a tenant does.

parts.note: a plain statement of someone having money still to pay back

explanation.surface: A simple report that someone has borrowed and not repaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has money outstanding to a creditor is said to be under that obligation.

parts.note: saws are read as tools, but here they are old sayings, which have no cutting teeth

explanation.surface: A carpenter complains that his blades are blunt.
explanation.walkthrough: A saw is also a proverb, the toothless kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Saws in the sense of proverbs or maxims are the same as wise traditional sayings.

clue.text: The Queen-of Carthage lends her name to slang pranks.

definitions.text: The Queen-of Carthage lends her name to slang pranks.

parts.words: The Queen-of Carthage lends her name to slang pranks
parts.note: Dido, Queen of Carthage in Virgil, gives a slang word for mischief or capers

explanation.surface: A historical note on a classical queen's name.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'cut didoes' is old American slang for playing tricks; Dido was the legendary Queen of Carthage.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang these are pranks or capers, named after the Carthaginian queen.

clue.text: This will make you lament, especially if you knock your head on it.

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are to be made into a new word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that a low shelf above the fire will hurt anyone who bangs into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will make you' rearranges the letters of 'lament'; 'This' and 'it' point to the shelf you hit your head on.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelf over a fireplace sticks out at head height, the thing one strikes with one's head.

parts.note: Punch was a British humorous weekly; E. V. Knox, its editor, wrote under a pseudonym

explanation.surface: A signature in a humour magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch was a famous British comic magazine; its editor E. V. Knox signed his pieces with this pen-name.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Knox, editor of Punch, signed his humorous verse with this Bacchic cry as a pseudonym.

parts.note: Rotten Row is the riding track in Hyde Park, London, where people go out on horseback

explanation.surface: A remark about what happens on a famous London bridle path.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotten Row is a sandy horse-riding track along Hyde Park in London; one takes a trip on horseback there.
explanation.definitionFit: Outings on horseback are what riders take along that London bridleway.

clue.text: I mean to wander; remove my heart to keep me at home.

definitions.text: I mean to wander; remove my heart to keep me at home.

parts.note: the word speaks: it means to roam, and with its middle letter taken out it becomes a word meaning remain

explanation.surface: A restless person says only losing their heart would keep them home.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the central R leaves STAY, which is what 'keep me at home' describes.
explanation.definitionFit: To go astray or roam about is to wander from where one belongs.

parts.note: echoes Macbeth's 'make assurance double sure', the comparative of sure

explanation.surface: Someone double-checks a guarantee.
explanation.walkthrough: It echoes Macbeth's line 'I'll make assurance double sure'.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative form means more certain, a doubled degree of sureness.

parts.note: nonsense, foolish talk

parts.note: lyric poems written in praise of a person or thing

parts.note: the five large freshwater lakes on the US–Canada border

explanation.surface: Naming a body of water in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Huron is the second largest of North America's five Great Lakes.

parts.note: a safe harbour feels blissful, and the word looks like heaven

explanation.surface: A traveller's relief at reaching shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for a harbour differs from 'heaven' by one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A refuge or safe harbour is a place of shelter that feels blessed to reach.

parts.note: in Britain a public school is an old fee-paying independent school

explanation.surface: A heading for a famous English school.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'public school' is a private fee-paying school; Eton College near Windsor is the best known.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is the most famous of the English fee-paying boarding schools.

definitions.meaning: an older person, one of greater age or rank
a small tree with white flowers and dark berries

explanation.surface: An old tree described as a pensioner.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an older person and also the shrub-like tree with dark berries.

clue.text: A wink would do as well.

definitions.text: A wink would do as well.

parts.words: A wink would do as well
parts.note: echoes the saying that one silent signal is as good as another to someone who understands

explanation.surface: A remark that a knowing signal would be enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying is 'a nod's as good as a wink'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip of the head is the gesture the proverb pairs with a wink as equally clear signals.

parts.note: Charlotte Corday stabbed a French revolutionary in his bath in 1793

explanation.surface: A historical fact about a famous assassination.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR splits 'Corday'; Jean-Paul Marat was murdered in his bath by her.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Marat, the radical journalist of the French Revolution, was stabbed by Charlotte Corday.

parts.note: the beat of poetic feet, the units of rhythm in a verse line

explanation.surface: A footprint left by someone walking.
explanation.walkthrough: Foot means a unit of verse rhythm, not a walker's foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhythmic pattern of verse is measured in feet, so it marks their fall.

parts.note: leeches were used by doctors to draw off a patient's blood

explanation.surface: The job of a bloodsucking worm, or of an old-time physician.
explanation.walkthrough: Leech is also an old word for a doctor, whose treatment was to let blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing blood was the work done by medicinal leeches and by doctors once called leeches.

clue.text: This, anagrammatically, is the name of the beast.

indicators.note: says the letters of the following word are rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A remark about naming an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anagrammatically' rearranges 'beast'; the result is a common English surname.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common English surname, so a name is all the definition offers.

parts.note: a surface cut at a slant rather than flat

explanation.surface: A builder's verdict on a crooked shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer differs from 'level' only in its first two letters, which is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloping edge cut at an angle to a surface is, by design, off the horizontal.

clue.text: Some people have the face to show this.

definitions.text: Some people have the face to show this.

parts.note: a reddening of the cheeks from shame, which bold people lack

explanation.surface: A dig at the shameless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have the face' means are bold, but the redness shows on the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddening of the face from shame or modesty shows on the cheeks.

parts.note: the usual short, familiar name children use for their male parent

explanation.surface: A family's casual name for the head of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The familiar word is a clipped, everyday form children use for their father.

explanation.surface: A pupil quickly tires of memorising history.
explanation.walkthrough: SATED rearranges into the answer: historical dates, or fruit a boy gorges on.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical years learnt by heart, or the sweet fruit of a palm, both bear this name.

clue.text: Here we find change in the songbook.

definitions.text: Here we find change in the songbook.

explanation.definitionFit: The book of psalms used in church services is a collection of sacred songs.

parts.note: people who love their nation, not the countryside

explanation.walkthrough: Country means nation, not rural land.
explanation.definitionFit: People devoted to their native land are lovers of their country.

parts.note: a radio set, though called wireless, still needs cables and aerials

explanation.definitionFit: Lengths of metal conductor are needed in a radio set despite its name.

clue.text: Ours is red on the map.

definitions.text: Ours is red on the map.

parts.words: Ours is red on the map
parts.note: British colonial maps coloured the lands under British rule red or pink

explanation.surface: A patriotic glance at an atlas.
explanation.walkthrough: Maps of the 1930s coloured the British Empire red.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of territories under one ruler; Britain's was shown in red on maps.

parts.note: glass containers with narrow necks that snap

definitions.text: This is seen out at the back.

clue.text: A fool or a tool does this.

clue.text: This sort of copying is a monkey trick.

definitions.text: This sort of copying is a monkey trick.

parts.note: imitating someone is likened to how primates mimic

clue.text: This discloses the weighty beginning of reparation.

definitions.text: This discloses the weighty beginning of reparation.

parts.words: This discloses the weighty beginning of reparation
parts.note: the word begins with A TON, something weighty, and means making amends

clue.text: If it's wrong you can get it out with this.

definitions.text: If it's wrong you can get it out with this.

parts.words: If it's wrong you can get it out with this
parts.note: a rubber removes a mistake from paper

explanation.surface: Advice about fixing a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber or similar tool removes wrongly written marks from paper.

parts.note: one word means both a hurry and a marsh plant with hollow stems

parts.note: spots as places, which are sometimes eyesores spoiling the view

parts.note: a covered chair borne on poles by two porters called chairmen

parts.note: a cook keeps a pan's contents moving with a spoon so they don't catch

explanation.surface: Advice for a cook watching a pot.

parts.note: the European quarter across the Golden Horn, now Beyoglu in Istanbul

parts.note: the plant life of a region is always paired with its animal life

explanation.walkthrough: The usual pairing is 'flora and fauna', the plants and animals of a place.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant life of a region is routinely named alongside its animal life, fauna.

parts.note: an archaic word for a mate, used by Edmund Spenser

explanation.surface: A friend from The Faerie Queene.

parts.note: as a verb, held a view or offered a belief

parts.words: This 'is a bit of a twister it depends on the thread

explanation.surface: A dishonest character whose story hangs by a thread.
explanation.walkthrough: Twister suggests a cheat, and thread a plot; really it is turned on a bolt's thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A small threaded metal block screwed on to a bolt to fasten it.

parts.note: large fishing nets with wide meshes that small fish slip through

explanation.surface: Tiny fish wriggle free of the fishermen's gear.
explanation.definitionFit: These large vertical fishing nets, hung with floats and weights, have meshes too coarse for minnows.

indicators.note: only a small piece of the next word is taken

parts.note: a breath or subtle emanation given off by something

clue.text: If the stakes are high at this card-game the loser may find himself in the middle of it.

parts.note: dried pale grapes without pips

explanation.definitionFit: These pale dried grapes from seedless varieties are used in baking.

parts.note: the comparative form of little, meaning smaller or of lower rank
